analysis.title: GS ETF Color: Inflows into levered ETFs
key_insights: The SOX index had its worst week of 2026 (-11%) and its second worst behind Liberation Day.
SMH has traded lower for 9 consecutive sessions, the longest downward streak in its 15-year history.
SPY, XLK and QQQ have outperformed SMH for 10 straight sessions, despite index overlaps with SMH of 20%, 37% and 45%.
Nearly $10 billion flowed into levered ETFs last week, the largest weekly inflow in GS's dataset.
SOXL (3x semis) gathered a record +$7 billion, 74% of weekly net inflows. TQQQ (3x NDX) was second at +$1.3 billion.
Levered ETF flows are historically strongest on days of sharp market declines (-2σ) and weakest on the best days (+2σ). Flows are also larger in absolute size during steep declines.
Last week's inflows pushed cumulative YTD levered ETF flows close to net positive. GS says the larger number of invested units could multiply gross levered exposure if market conditions improve.
Levered ETFs hold $152 billion in AUM and $386 billion in gross exposure, the second-lowest gross exposure since July.
risk_factors: Continued semiconductor weakness after record inflows into 3x semis (SOXL) leaves those holders exposed to further losses.
A rebound could be amplified by the larger base of invested levered ETF units, per GS.
vol_and_positioning: Record levered ETF inflows (~$10B in one week) came during a semis sell-off, consistent with the historical pattern of buying declines in this complex.
Levered ETF gross exposure is $386 billion on $152 billion AUM, the second-lowest since July.
Cumulative YTD levered ETF flows are near net-positive, so more invested units could amplify gross exposure if the market recovers.
